related_questions.question: What would cause a person to get shingles?
related_questions.snippet: People get shingles when the varicella-zoster virus (VZV), which causes chickenpox, reactivates in their bodies after they have already had chickenpox. An estimated 1 million people get shingles each year in this country. Most people who develop shingles only have it one time during their life.

related_questions.question: Is it safe to be around someone with shingles?

text_blocks.snippet: It is generally safe to be around someone with shingles, but it's important to be aware of potential risks for those who haven't had chickenpox or the chickenpox vaccine. Shingles itself is not contagious, but the varicella-zoster virus (VZV) that causes shingles can be spread to individuals who have never had chickenpox or the chickenpox vaccine, causing them to develop chickenpox, not shingles.

list.title: Shingles cannot be directly transmitted:
list.snippet: You cannot catch shingles from someone who has shingles.

list.title: Chickenpox can be spread:
list.snippet: The varicella-zoster virus (VZV), the same virus that causes chickenpox, can be spread through direct contact with fluid from shingles blisters.

list.title: Risk to vulnerable individuals:
list.snippet: People who are at higher risk from chickenpox complications, such as infants, pregnant women, and those with weakened immune systems, should avoid contact with anyone experiencing a shingles outbreak, especially when blisters are present.

list.title: When shingles is contagious:
list.snippet: A person with shingles is contagious while their blisters are oozing fluid (weeping) and until the blisters have dried and scabbed over.

list.title: Precautions:
list.snippet: To minimize the risk of spreading the virus, individuals with shingles should:
Keep the rash covered.
Avoid touching the rash.
Wash their hands frequently.
Avoid close contact with individuals who have never had chickenpox or the chickenpox vaccine.

text_blocks.snippet: Shingles is a viral infection caused by the varicella-zoster virus, the same virus that causes chickenpox. After a person has chickenpox, the virus remains dormant in the body, and can reactivate later in life as shingles, causing a painful rash. While there's no cure for shingles, early antiviral treatment can shorten the duration and severity of the infection, and help prevent complications.
snippet_highlighted_words: early antiviral treatment can shorten the duration and severity of the infection, and help prevent complications

list.title: Chickenpox:
list.snippet: Shingles is caused by the reactivation of the varicella-zoster virus, which is the same virus that causes chickenpox.

list.title: Weakened Immune System:
list.snippet: The virus can reactivate when the immune system is weakened, which can happen with age, stress, certain illnesses, or medications.

list.title: Age:
list.snippet: The risk of shingles increases with age, with about half of all cases occurring in people aged 60 and older.

list.title: Antiviral Medications:
list.snippet: Antiviral drugs like acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir can help reduce the pain, shorten the course of the illness, and decrease the risk of complications.

list.title: Pain Relief:
list.snippet: Over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen or acetaminophen can help manage mild pain. Stronger prescription pain medications, such as opioids or nerve pain medications (like gabapentin or amitriptyline), may be necessary for more severe pain.

list.title: Topical Treatments:
list.snippet: Creams or lotions can help soothe the itching and pain associated with the rash. Capsaicin cream may also be helpful for nerve pain.

list.title: Other Medications:
list.snippet: Corticosteroids may be used to reduce inflammation and pain. Antibiotics may be needed if a bacterial infection develops at the site of the rash.

list.title: Home Care:
list.snippet: Cool compresses, calamine lotion, and rest can help manage symptoms.

list.title: Early Treatment is Key:
list.snippet: Antiviral medications are most effective when started within 72 hours of the first symptoms (tingling or pain).

list.title: Preventing Shingles:
list.snippet: The shingles vaccine (Shingrix) is recommended for adults 50 years and older to help prevent shingles and its complications, according to the CDC.

list.title: Potential Complications:
list.snippet: Shingles can lead to postherpetic neuralgia (long-term nerve pain), vision loss (if it affects the eye), or other complications, especially in those with weakened immune systems.
